steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Skill: A learned action with a predetermined result that can be reproduced consistently with minimum effort and time. Skills are developed through practice and experience. | Ability: An innate, inherited trait that underpins skilled performance. Abilities are the building blocks of skills and are largely genetically determined. | Exam Tip: Most skills fall somewhere between the two extremes. A netball chest pass is basic, but adding a defender and deciding when to pass makes it more complex. Context matters. | Key Principle: The more open and externally paced a skill is, the more decision-making is required. Practice should therefore include game-like situations. Closed, self-paced skills can be practised in isolated, repetitive drills.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Define the terms 'skill' and 'ability' and explain the relationship between them. | Using a named sporting example, explain the difference between an open skill and a closed skill. | Classify a golf drive using all four skill classification continua.
